tasks.output: Proof-of-work and proof-of-stake are two ways cryptocurrencies confirm transactions and secure their networks. Proof-of-work requires computers to solve complex puzzles, using a lot of electricity, to add new blocks to the blockchain. This process is competitive and rewards those who solve puzzles first. Proof-of-stake, on the other hand, selects validators based on how many coins they hold and are willing to "stake" or lock up as a guarantee. It uses far less energy because it doesn't rely on heavy computing. Proof-of-work is more energy-intensive but has been proven secure over time, while proof-of-stake is more energy-efficient and scalable but is newer. Both aim to keep transactions secure and trustworthy but differ mainly in how they achieve this goal.
